title: Chicago, summer 1835

lighting.note: Early afternoon, 1 July 1835. Sun azimuth and elevation are computed from this time and the datum lat/lon and drive both sky and the single directional light. Chosen so the south elevation is genuinely lit — at this latitude in July the sun is high, so vertical surfaces take light at a grazing angle and a mid-morning sun leaves a south wall too dark to read its documented white paint.

anchors.label: The Sauganash Hotel, Lake and Market
The log wing, from the south-west
Fort Dearborn and the river mouth

note: The first scene. Population roughly 3,265 in the late-1835 count; the town is twenty months old and has grown roughly tenfold in two years. Wabansia and Kinzie's Addition are platted (the Wooley correction was approved 17 June 1835, two weeks before this date) but almost entirely unbuilt. Anchor coordinates are provisional until the datum is verified — they are placeholders in the same local frame, not survey positions. Spawn and the near anchors stand south of the Sauganash looking north at its front elevation; they were previously at the origin, which is inside the building. Distant anchors remain provisional until those structures are placed.
